title: Riyadh Airport Status October 2026: Latest Updates and Travel Advice
meta_title: Riyadh Airport Status October 2026: Latest Updates
meta_description: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has been disrupted since 10 October 2026. What GACA has announced, what to check, and onward travel options.
excerpt: GACA suspended operations at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport after an attack on 10 October 2026. What has been officially announced, what remains unconfirmed, and what travellers should do now.
content:
Last updated: 22 October 2026. This is a developing situation. Check your airline and the official sources listed below before you travel.

Short answer: Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) suspended operations at King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh after an attack on the afternoon of Saturday 10 October 2026; the airport was struck again on Sunday 11 October. On 12 October, GACA extended the suspension to complete checks on the safety and operational readiness of the airport's facilities, without giving an end date. A NOTAM reported by Reuters on 12 October set a closure period ending at 21:00 UTC on Saturday 17 October. Since then, reports have differed: aviation press reported a new notice from 17 October requiring prior GACA permission for all flights, while other outlets reported that the airport remained closed. As of 22 October 2026, we have not found an official GACA announcement that scheduled passenger flights have resumed. Do not go to the airport unless your airline has confirmed your flight is operating.

For the separate incidents at Dammam's King Fahd International Airport on 11 and 21 October, see our Dammam airport advisory.

What Happened at Riyadh Airport

Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said the airport was targeted in an attack on the afternoon of 10 October and that operations were "temporarily suspended pending a full damage assessment", while the safety of its facilities was verified. According to Saudi authorities as reported by Asharq Al-Awsat and The National, the attack killed 12 people and injured 309. On 11 October, India's embassy said one of its citizens had died of injuries sustained in that attack, which the Associated Press reported would bring the toll to 13.

On Sunday 11 October, a projectile struck a passenger terminal at the airport again. GACA confirmed the death of a Pakistani resident and injuries to 11 others in that second attack, according to NBC News.

Yemen's Houthis have claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi airports, according to the Associated Press; GACA's own statements did not name those responsible. These strikes followed an earlier attack on the same airport on 8 October, after which GACA said air traffic had returned to normal on 9 October.

Current Status at a Glance

ItemStatus as of 22 October 2026
AirportKing Khalid International Airport (RUH), Riyadh
OperationsSuspended by GACA on the afternoon of 10 October 2026; the airport was struck again on 11 October, and GACA extended the suspension on 12 October for safety and operational-readiness checks. We have not found a later official GACA statement on operations
Announced byGeneral Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA)
Aviation notices (as reported)A NOTAM reported by Reuters on 12 October set a closure period ending 21:00 UTC (midnight Riyadh time) on 17 October. Aviation press reported that a new NOTAM, A3650/26, effective from 18:45 UTC on 17 October, requires prior GACA permission for all departing and arriving traffic (Inside Aviation, 18 October)
ReopeningNot officially confirmed. Reports since 17 October differ — some describe a limited reopening under prior permission, others continued closure. Check your flight with your airline
FlightsFlightradar24 listed more than 500 flights to and from Riyadh as cancelled on Monday 12 October, according to The National. Across all Saudi airports, Cirium data showed 486 of 1,048 scheduled departures cancelled or not operated by 16:00 that day, according to Air Data News
DiversionsOn 10 October, inbound flights diverted mainly to Jeddah, according to Flightradar24 data reported by Gulf News. Time Out Riyadh reported on 21 October that flights were being diverted to Madinah and Qassim

What This Means for Flights

Airlines decide individually when to cancel or restart Riyadh services. In the days after 10 October, several carriers — including Etihad, Emirates, flydubai, Air Arabia and EgyptAir — cancelled or suspended Riyadh flights, according to The National, and Air Data News reported on 12 October that the Lufthansa Group and Air France-KLM had suspended Riyadh flights for longer periods. Later reports said some airlines had pushed their return into November or 2027. Airline plans change frequently, so check your own airline rather than relying on these reports.

Even after an official reopening, schedules may take time to recover. After the 9 October reopening, hundreds of flights remained delayed or cancelled, and individual airlines decide when to restart their own Riyadh services.

What Travellers Should Do Now

  • Don't go to the airport unless your airline has confirmed that your specific flight is operating.
  • Check your flight with your airline directly, through its app, website or the booking reference sent to you, rather than relying on general schedules.
  • Ask about rebooking and refunds. If your flight is cancelled, contact your airline or travel agent about your options, which may include rerouting through another Saudi airport.
  • Follow official safety guidance. Follow instructions from Saudi authorities, including Civil Defense alerts. Several governments, including the United States, have advised their citizens to avoid the airport and its surrounding areas.
  • Register with your embassy if your government offers a registration service for citizens abroad.
  • Keep documents and essentials with you — passport, booking references, medication and phone charger — in case plans change at short notice.

If Your Airline Reroutes You Through Another Airport

If your airline rebooks you through another Saudi airport, you may need ground transport to or from Riyadh. Only make road plans once your new flight is confirmed, and follow official guidance on travel at the time. Air Data News reported on 12 October that there is no general Saudi government programme transferring passengers from Riyadh to alternative airports, so any rerouting is arranged by your airline. Note that Dammam's King Fahd International Airport was attacked on 11 October and again on the evening of 21 October; on 22 October GACA said operations there had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal (as reported by Arab News). See our Dammam airport advisory and check your flight before relying on it.

We can quote road transfers to or from Riyadh for these airports — each journey is confirmed in a quotation before you travel:

  • Qassim (including Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport) to Riyadh
  • Dammam Airport to Riyadh
  • Madinah Airport to Riyadh
  • Jeddah Airport to Riyadh

Between Dammam and Riyadh there is also a SAR passenger rail service — check SAR directly for current schedules and availability. For planning help, see our guide to arranging an intercity transfer during flight disruptions.

Airport Transfers to and from Riyadh Airport

We are not confirming pickups or drop-offs at King Khalid International Airport in advance while its operations are disrupted; any airport pickup or drop-off is confirmed case by case in your quotation. If you've booked a Riyadh airport transfer with us, message us with your airline's latest update and we'll review the booking with you, or quote the new journey if your airline has rebooked you through a different airport. No payment is needed to receive a quote.

Official and News Sources

  • General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) — statement on the suspension of operations, published by the Saudi Press Agency
  • Asharq Al-Awsat — GACA statement and casualty figures, 10 October 2026
  • The Associated Press (via CP24) — second strike and revised toll, 11 October 2026
  • NBC News — GACA figures for the 11 October strike
  • The National — closure extension and airline cancellations, updated 12 October 2026
  • General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) — suspension extended for safety checks, published by the Saudi Press Agency, 12 October 2026
  • Reuters (via The Times of Israel) — NOTAM keeping the airport closed until 21:00 UTC on 17 October, 12 October 2026
  • Air Data News — airline suspensions and Cirium data, 12 October 2026
  • Inside Aviation — NOTAM A3650/26 (prior GACA permission for all traffic from 17 October), 18 October 2026
  • Time Out Riyadh — airport status and diversions, updated 21 October 2026
  • Arab News — GACA statement on Dammam airport operations, 22 October 2026
  • Your airline's official website or app — the authoritative source for your own flight

This article summarises official statements and reliable reporting available on 22 October 2026. It is not official guidance. We will update it when a significant official announcement changes the situation.

Need to Change a Transfer?

If your travel plans around Riyadh have changed, send us your new flight details and we'll reply with a quotation for the journey you now need — the confirmed quotation sets the price — or review an existing booking with you. See our Riyadh Airport page for current guidance.
